Chapter 9. Bearing Witness Today: The Power of Story
Imagine a journalist, haunted by the images he’s seen. He sits at his desk, struggling to find words powerful enough to capture the horror he’s witnessed. He writes, then rewrites, knowing that every sentence carries a heavy responsibility. There’s this nagging question—will anyone care? Will the world even listen? But he keeps going, fueled by the belief that staying silent just isn’t an option.
Then, years after Leopold’s rule has ended, a survivor stands before a classroom, sharing her story with a group of schoolchildren. Her voice trembles, but there’s a quiet strength in the way she speaks. She isn’t trying to frighten them, or make them angry. She just wants them to understand that their lives are deeply connected to those who came before. For her, memory isn’t just about looking back—it’s a form of resistance. It’s how she honors those who were lost, and protects those who are still here.
Bearing witness—it’s never easy, is it? It takes real courage, deep empathy, and a willingness to face truths that are anything but comfortable. Yet, in the middle of all that struggle, there’s hope. Telling these stories reminds us that, even in the darkest moments, the human spirit can endure—and even prevail.
